message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"2.45","text":"Therefore, child Clement, be on guard not to think anything about God other than that he alone is God and Lord and Father, good and just, creator, patient, merciful, nourisher, benefactor, practicing benevolence toward humanity, counseling purity, eternal and making people eternal, incomparable, dwelling in the souls of the good, uncontainable yet contained; the one who fixed the great world within the boundless like a center point, who spread out heaven and compressed the earth, stored up water, arranged stars in heaven, made springs gush in the earth, made fruits spring up, raised mountains, set bounds around the sea, and ordered winds and spirits; the one who secured the encompassing body in a boundless sea by “spirit of counsel.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"φιλανθρωπίαν’ νομιτεύων","chosen":"practicing benevolence toward humanity","rationale":"The rare νομιτεύων is understood in the sense of observing or practicing something as customary; alternatively, the phrase could mean “making benevolence toward humanity his rule.”"},{"source_quote":"αἰώνιος, αἰωνίους ποιῶν","chosen":"eternal and making people eternal","rationale":"The first adjective describes God, while the masculine plural αἰωνίους supplies an implied personal object for the participle."},{"source_quote":"ἀχώρητος καὶ χωρούμενος","chosen":"uncontainable yet contained","rationale":"The rendering retains the source’s deliberate paradox; χωρούμενος may also carry the sense “received” or “comprehended.”"},{"source_quote":"ὁ ἐν ἀπείρῳ τὸν μέγαν αἰῶνα ὡς κέντρον πήξας","chosen":"the one who fixed the great world within the boundless like a center point","rationale":"Although αἰών can mean “age” or “aeon,” the spatial language of fixing it in the boundless as a κέντρον supports the cosmological rendering “world.”"},{"source_quote":"γῆν πιλώσας","chosen":"compressed the earth","rationale":"πιλόω depicts pressing or compacting, with an underlying image of material being felted together."},{"source_quote":"τὸ περιέχον σῶμα ἐν ἀπείρῳ πελάγει „πνεύματι βουλῆς“ ἀσφαλισάμενος","chosen":"secured the encompassing body in a boundless sea by “spirit of counsel”","rationale":"πνεύματι is taken instrumentally and ἐν ἀπείρῳ πελάγει locally. The participle περιέχον may describe a body that encompasses or surrounds all things."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"φιλανθρωπίαν’ νομιτεύων","issue":"The printed apostrophe after φιλανθρωπίαν has no evident elision or syntactic function, and νομιτεύων is rare. The clause remains defensibly renderable without changing its letters.","proposed_reading":"φιλανθρωπίαν νομιτεύων","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"2.46","text":"He is our judge. Looking to him, we must set our own souls right, considering everything with reference to him, praising him, and being convinced that, while by his patience he brings everyone’s recklessness into the open, he alone is good. And at the end of all things, he will take his seat before each of those who have dared what they should not have as a just judge.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"πάντα ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ νοοῦντας","chosen":"considering everything with reference to him","rationale":"With νοεῖν, ὑπέρ can indicate the reference or concern governing one’s thought; “considering everything for his sake” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"αὐτὸν εὐφημοῦντας","chosen":"praising him","rationale":"εὐφημέω literally concerns speaking well of someone and here functions as praise directed to God."},{"source_quote":"τῇ αὐτοῦ μακροθυμίᾳ πάντων τὴν προπέτειαν εἰς φανερὸν ἄγων","chosen":"while by his patience he brings everyone’s recklessness into the open","rationale":"The dative may be instrumental, “by his patience,” or modal, “in his patience.” The participle is rendered circumstantially without making its precise logical relationship exclusively causal."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ τέλει τοῦ παντὸς","chosen":"at the end of all things","rationale":"τοῦ παντός can denote the totality of things or the universe; the final-judgment context supports “all things,” while “at the end of the universe” remains possible."},{"source_quote":"προκαθεσθήσεται κριτής","chosen":"will take his seat ... as a just judge","rationale":"The verb presents the judge as being seated before those judged; “will preside as judge” is a smoother alternative."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"2.47","text":"After hearing these things, I, Clement, said, “Truly, this is reverence for God; this truly is piety.” Then I said again, “So I would like to learn why the books were written in this way. For I remember you saying that it was to expose those who would dare to believe anything said against God. Still, since you graciously allow us to question you as we wish, we venture to question you, since you have instructed us to do so. If someone should wish, dearest Peter, to say to us, ‘What has been written is true, even if what has been said against God seems false to you,’ how are we to answer him?”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"θεοσέβεια ... εὐσέβεια","chosen":"reverence for God ... piety","rationale":"The rendering distinguishes explicit reverence directed toward God from the broader quality of devout or pious conduct."},{"source_quote":"εἰς ἔλεγχον τῶν μελλόντων τολμᾶν πιστεύειν","chosen":"to expose those who would dare to believe","rationale":"ἔλεγχος can denote exposure, testing, refutation, or conviction. “Expose” fits the claim that such readers reveal themselves by believing statements against God."},{"source_quote":"χαρίζῃ ἡμῖν πυνθάνεσθαί σου ὡς βουλόμεθα","chosen":"you graciously allow us to question you as we wish","rationale":"χαρίζῃ presents the permission as a favor, while ὡς βουλόμεθα describes the freedom with which they may ask."},{"source_quote":"κἂν σοὶ ψευδῆ δοκῇ τὰ κατὰ τοῦ θεοῦ ῥηθέντα","chosen":"even if what has been said against God seems false to you","rationale":"The rendering preserves both the concessive force of κἄν and the subjective appearance expressed by σοὶ ... δοκῇ, rather than asserting directly that the statements are false."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"2.48","text":"Peter answered, “You did well to ask, for it will be for your security. But listen. Since many things have been said against God by the writings, in view of the hour’s urgency because of the evening, ask about whichever one statement you wish, and I will resolve it, showing it to be false not merely because it has been stated against God, but because it is actually false.” And I replied, “I want to learn how, when the writings say that God does not know, you can prove that he does know.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὰ ὑπὸ τῶν γραφῶν εἰρημένα","chosen":"things ... said ... by the writings","rationale":"γραφαί can be rendered “Scriptures,” but “writings” preserves the lexical form without imposing a capitalization or canonical designation not marked by the Greek."},{"source_quote":"πρὸς τὸ ἐπεῖγον τῆς ὥρας διὰ τὴν ἑσπέραν","chosen":"in view of the hour’s urgency because of the evening","rationale":"The phrase attributes the pressure of the available time to the evening; a smoother alternative is “since evening makes the time pressing.”"},{"source_quote":"ἕνα ὃν βούλει λόγον πυθοῦ","chosen":"ask about whichever one statement you wish","rationale":"λόγος here denotes a particular assertion or passage to be questioned rather than speech in general."},{"source_quote":"οὐχ ὅτι μόνον κατὰ τοῦ θεοῦ εἴρηται, ἀλλ’ ὅτι ὄντως ψευδής ἐστιν","chosen":"not merely because it has been stated against God, but because it is actually false","rationale":"The contrast denies that opposition to God alone is the ground for rejection and promises a demonstration of the statement’s actual falsehood."},{"source_quote":"ἀγνοεῖν λεγουσῶν τὸν θεὸν ... γινώσκοντα αὐτὸν ἀποδεῖξαι","chosen":"say that God does not know ... prove that he does know","rationale":"The repeated English verb preserves the direct contrast between ἀγνοεῖν and γινώσκοντα without supplying an unstated object of God’s knowledge."}],"source_issues":[]}]}
